why: Builds the CI guard BL-20260814-HAND-RESOLVED-BACKLOG-MERGE-SILENTLY-REVERTED-SIX-ITEMS-INCLUDING-A-RESOLUTION asks for, and closes that row. scripts/ci/check_backlog_unresolve.py grades TWO regressions diff-scoped against --base, in the criterion's own words: (1) a row's `status` moving from a TERMINAL value to a LIVE one; (2) a POPULATED `resolved_at` being emptied. Registered in scripts/ci/run_guards.py as `backlog-unresolve-guard` with `when: None` — a regression is written by whoever last touches a backlog file, and the whole run costs ~1.0s (measured: 749ms self-test + 268ms base run), so there is nothing to buy by scoping it. IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE, VERIFIED BEFORE BUILDING: the sibling `register-field-loss-guard` catches a field DISAPPEARING, not a field's VALUE regressing, so it is structurally blind to both conditions here; grep for terminal-status / resolved_at regression logic across scripts/ci/ returned nothing. TERMINALITY IS NOT RE-DERIVED — it is read from the single canonical owner, scripts/reports/backlog_counts.py::is_open_status, loaded by path and memoised. A second definition of 'which rows are live' would BE the defect one level up, and the guard's own self-test pins the two sets apart. ITEM COUNT IS CHECKED NOWHERE IN IT, which the criterion explicitly forbids ('Item COUNT is not a sufficient invariant and must not be what the guard checks') — and is precisely why the 2026-08-14 incident was invisible: six rows were reverted and the count never moved. THE ESCAPE HATCH REQUIRES A FRESH REASON, NOT A PRESENT ONE. The criterion says 'unless the same commit records why', so `reopen_reason`/`reopened_reason` must have CHANGED against base, or the `reopened_at`+`reopened_by` pair must have changed. A stale reason left from a previous re-open grants nothing, and a planted control pins that — otherwise a row re-opened once carries a permanent licence to be re-opened silently forever. STATE THE POPULATION ON THE EVIDENCE, because it is weaker than it could be and that is said here rather than implied: the basis is TEN PLANTED CONTROLS in `--self-test` (temp git repos, graded in BOTH directions — a silent re-open FAILS, a re-open with a fresh reason passes, a stale reason grants nothing, the reopened_at+reopened_by pair is accepted when fresh, clearing a populated resolved_at FAILS, an untouched closed row is CLEAN, an ordinary open row edited in place is CLEAN, a row closed IN this diff is CLEAN), 10/10 passing. A REAL-HISTORY POSITIVE CONTROL WAS ATTEMPTED AND IS NOT AVAILABLE: the incident commit c601d82e is not in this clone (shallow/gone), so the guard has never been shown firing on the actual reversion it was built for. The planted controls are the whole basis. Running clean over origin/main and over ~40, ~200 and ~600 commits of real history establishes it does not false-positive on this corpus; that is a negative control, not a positive one, and is not quoted as one. Filed through scripts/ops/backlog_append.py::update_row, never by hand — the backlog edit is 11 insertions / 2 deletions, so the byte-exact round-trip held and no pre-existing row was re-attributed to this PR.
